title: ～だけ — “only ～”
summary: Attaches to a word and limits the range to just that, with nothing else. It follows nouns and quantities, and also the plain form of verbs and adjectives.

patterns.gloss: Right after a noun or quantity (水だけ, 少しだけ, 一人だけ)

patterns.form: 動詞・形容詞の普通形＋だけ
patterns.gloss: Plain form + だけ (e.g. 見るだけ “just look”)

body.p: It narrows things down to just the item named. 水だけください means “water and nothing else.”

body.h: How it fits in a sentence
body.p: The particles が and を are often dropped after だけ (水だけください). Others such as は, に, で can follow it (私だけは, ここでだけ).
だけ is neutral and goes with an affirmative sentence. しか must be paired with a negative and often suggests “that is all, and it is not enough.”

examples.ja: 今日（きょう）は少（すこ）しだけ食（た）べました。
examples.tr: I ate only a little today.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもは一人（ひとり）だけです。

pitfalls: Keep だけ in an affirmative sentence. Do not mix up 水しかありません and 水だけあります.
ばかり and のみ are different words. In everyday speech the basic choice is だけ.
